quests.instruction: Look carefully! Which animal has scaly skin and a long tail?
quests.hint: This animal usually lives sunbathing on a warm desert rock.
quests.explanation: That's right! The lizard has scaly skin and a long tail. You can find it sunbathing on a warm desert rock.
quests.funFact: Some lizards can run on water using extremely fast footsteps.

quests.instruction: Which animal can trot quietly and pounce?
quests.hint: This animal lives creeping through the forest at dusk.
quests.explanation: Yes! The fox can trot quietly and pounce. It has a bushy tail and pointed ears.
quests.funFact: They have whiskers on their legs as well as their face.

quests.instruction: Which animal is NOT an amphibian?
quests.hint: Look for the animal that is a reptile instead.
quests.explanation: Well done! The snake is a reptile, not an amphibian. The other two animals are amphibians.
quests.funFact: They do not have eyelids; instead, they have a clear scale covering their eye.

quests.instruction: One of these animals is a bird. Which one?
quests.hint: This animal has long legs and the biggest eyes of any land animal.
quests.explanation: Yes! The ostrich is a bird. It lives running across the open plains.
quests.funFact: They lay the largest eggs of any living animal.

quests.instruction: A baby panda has a special name. What is it called?
quests.hint: Baby animal names are often short and sweet, just like round black and white patches.
quests.explanation: That's it! A baby panda is called a cub. Grown-up pandas live munching bamboo in a misty forest.
quests.funFact: A baby bear, lion, or tiger is called a cub.

quests.instruction: I have strong back legs and a built-in baby pouch. I live hopping across the land in Australia. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is a mammal.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the kangaroo! It has strong back legs and a built-in baby pouch and lives hopping across the land in Australia.
quests.funFact: They are the only large animals that use hopping as their primary movement.

quests.instruction: Look carefully. Which animal here is an insect?
quests.hint: This animal has a tiny body and super strong legs.
quests.explanation: Yes! The ant is an insect. It lives marching through the garden.
quests.funFact: Ants don't have lungs; they breathe through tiny holes all over their bodies.

quests.instruction: A group of ostriches has a special name. What is it?
quests.hint: Think about where ostriches usually live: running across the open plains.
quests.explanation: Yes! A group of ostriches is called a flock. They like to stay together running across the open plains.
quests.funFact: Flocks of starlings can create incredible swirling patterns in the sky.

quests.instruction: Listen closely! Who says "Croak"?
quests.hint: Think of an animal that lives hopping through a damp garden.
quests.explanation: Yes! A toad says "Croak". It also has dry, bumpy skin.
quests.funFact: Toads have dry, bumpy skin and prefer to walk rather than hop.

quests.instruction: Which animal can hop in short little jumps?
quests.hint: This animal lives hopping through a damp garden.
quests.explanation: Yes! The toad can hop in short little jumps. It has dry, bumpy skin.
quests.funFact: They secrete a bitter toxin from their skin to deter predators.

quests.instruction: Which animal has a see-through, umbrella-shaped body?
quests.hint: This animal usually lives drifting through the ocean water.
quests.explanation: That's right! The jellyfish has a see-through, umbrella-shaped body. You can find it drifting through the ocean water.
quests.funFact: Did you know? a group of jellyfish is hilariously called a smack.

quests.instruction: Who is able to float upright and drift slowly? Choose the right animal!
quests.hint: This animal lives drifting near ocean seaweed.
quests.explanation: Yes! The seahorse can float upright and drift slowly. It has a curly tail and a horse-shaped head.
quests.funFact: Did you know? male seahorses are the ones who carry and give birth to the babies.

quests.instruction: Can you find the animal that lives in a garden?
quests.hint: Look for the animal with hundreds of sharp little spines.
quests.explanation: Great job! The hedgehog lives in a garden. You can spot it by hundreds of sharp little spines.
quests.funFact: When scared, they roll into a tight, prickly ball.

quests.instruction: I have dry, bumpy skin. I live hopping through a damp garden. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is an amphibian.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the toad! It has dry, bumpy skin and lives hopping through a damp garden.
quests.funFact: Toads do not have teeth, so they swallow their prey whole.

quests.instruction: I have huge round eyes and silent wings. I live in a tree in a quiet forest. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is a bird.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the owl! It has huge round eyes and silent wings and lives in a tree in a quiet forest.
quests.funFact: They have special feathers that allow them to fly completely silently.

quests.instruction: Which animal is NOT an amphibian?
quests.hint: Look for the animal that is a mammal instead.
quests.explanation: Well done! The camel is a mammal, not an amphibian. The other two animals are amphibians.
quests.funFact: A camel can drink up to 40 gallons of water in a single sitting.

quests.instruction: A baby rhino has a special name. What is it called?
quests.hint: Baby animal names are often short and sweet, just like one or two horns and very thick skin.
quests.explanation: That's it! A baby rhino is called a calf. Grown-up rhinos live grazing on the open plains.
quests.funFact: A calf drinks milk from its mother until it is old enough to eat grass.

quests.instruction: Which animal makes its home in the jungle?
quests.hint: Look for the animal with very strong arms and a broad chest.
quests.explanation: Great job! The gorilla lives in the jungle. You can spot it by very strong arms and a broad chest.
quests.funFact: Gorillas are incredibly strong but generally very gentle herbivores.

quests.instruction: Which animal lives in the jungle?
quests.hint: Look for the animal with a giant fan of colorful tail feathers.
quests.explanation: Great job! The peacock lives in the jungle. You can spot it by a giant fan of colorful tail feathers.
quests.funFact: Did you know? only male peafowl are called peacocks; females are peahens.

quests.instruction: One of these animals lives in a river. Which one?
quests.hint: Look for the animal with long jaws and rows of sharp teeth.
quests.explanation: Great job! The crocodile lives in a river. You can spot it by long jaws and rows of sharp teeth.
quests.funFact: They cannot chew their food, so they swallow stones to help grind it up.

quests.instruction: Look carefully! Which animal has sharp teeth and thick grey fur?
quests.hint: This animal usually lives roaming through the forest.
quests.explanation: That's right! The wolf has sharp teeth and thick grey fur. It says "Howl".
quests.funFact: A wolf can run at speeds of up to 40 miles per hour during a chase.

quests.instruction: I have two pairs of colorful, patterned wings. I live fluttering over garden flowers. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is an insect.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the butterfly! It has two pairs of colorful, patterned wings and lives fluttering over garden flowers.
quests.funFact: A butterfly's wings are actually clear; the colors are just microscopic scales.

quests.instruction: I have a round red shell with black spots. I live resting on a garden leaf. What am I?
quests.hint: This animal is an insect.
quests.explanation: Yes, it's the ladybug! It has a round red shell with black spots and lives resting on a garden leaf.
quests.funFact: When it gets cold, ladybugs gather in large groups to hibernate.

quests.instruction: Two of these are amphibians. Which one is different?
quests.hint: Look for the animal that is a reptile instead.
quests.explanation: Well done! The turtle is a reptile, not an amphibian. The other two animals are amphibians.
quests.funFact: Turtles have been living on Earth since the time of the dinosaurs.

quests.instruction: Who is able to march in a busy line? Choose the right animal!
quests.hint: This animal lives marching through the garden.
quests.explanation: Yes! The ant can march in a busy line. It has a tiny body and super strong legs.
quests.funFact: Some queen ants can live for up to 30 years!

quests.instruction: Look carefully! Which animal has long jaws and rows of sharp teeth?
quests.hint: This animal usually lives floating quietly in a river.
quests.explanation: That's right! The crocodile has long jaws and rows of sharp teeth. You can find it floating quietly in a river.
quests.funFact: Crocodiles can hold their breath underwater for over an hour.

quests.instruction: Who is able to creep slowly along the seabed? Choose the right animal!
quests.hint: This animal lives resting on the ocean floor.
quests.explanation: Yes! The starfish can creep slowly along the seabed. It has five arms shaped like a star.
quests.funFact: They have tiny 'eyes' at the very tip of each arm to sense light.

quests.instruction: Where would you find this animal? Who lives in the desert?
quests.hint: Look for the animal with scaly skin and a long tail.
quests.explanation: Great job! The lizard lives in the desert. You can spot it by scaly skin and a long tail.
quests.funFact: Lizards smell their environment using their tongues.

quests.instruction: Two of these are amphibians. Which one is different?
quests.hint: Look for the animal that is a reptile instead.
quests.explanation: Well done! The crocodile is a reptile, not an amphibian. The other two animals are amphibians.
quests.funFact: They are ancient reptiles that lived alongside the dinosaurs.

quests.instruction: Which animal has tall branching antlers?
quests.hint: This animal usually lives grazing quietly in the forest.
quests.explanation: That's right! The deer has tall branching antlers. You can find it grazing quietly in the forest.
quests.funFact: A group of deer is called a herd.
